text: Ligand binding to a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) typically triggers which sequence of molecular events?
choices: GDP-GTP exchange on a Gα subunit, followed by dissociation of Gα-GTP from Gβγ
A conformational change in an IP3 receptor on the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, releasing calcium
Direct binding of the ligand to an intracellular nuclear receptor, followed by receptor dimerization and DNA binding
Ligand-induced receptor dimerization, transautophosphorylation of the activation loop, and recruitment of SH2-domain proteins to the resulting phosphotyrosines
explanation: RTK activation proceeds through ligand-induced dimerization of two receptor monomers, transautophosphorylation of each other's activation loops, and recruitment of SH2-domain-containing proteins to the newly created phosphotyrosines, which then activate downstream pathways such as RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT. Choice 0 describes GPCR signaling, an entirely different receptor class that uses heterotrimeric G proteins rather than intrinsic kinase activity. Choice 1 describes IP3-induced calcium release, and choice 2 describes nuclear hormone receptor signaling -- both distinct receptor mechanisms unrelated to RTK activation.
